subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: What should be the canonical plugin-visible payload and timing boundary for Codex-native shell/apply_patch `after_tool_call` observations?
rationale: The code can be repaired in several ways, but changing `after_tool_call.result` from a raw string to a structured object affects the public plugin SDK contract and must also choose the native-relay versus app-server projection dedupe boundary.

options.title: Structured Single Observation
options.body: Expose a structured object with text/status/exitCode metadata and make either app-server completion data or an enriched relay the single source of truth for Codex-native tools.

options.title: Add Parallel Structured Field
options.body: Keep `result` as the raw text for compatibility and add a new documented field such as `outcome` or `details` for status and exit-code data.

options.title: Keep Raw String Contract
options.body: Document that Codex-native `after_tool_call` is raw text only and leave plugins to use separate aggregate or trace surfaces for outcome data.

recommendation.title: Structured Single Observation
recommendation.body: Expose a structured object with text/status/exitCode metadata and make either app-server completion data or an enriched relay the single source of truth for Codex-native tools.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Codex native relay and app-server projection implementation traces to this owner in current-main history, and the decision is about that boundary.
